rationale:
Small, additive, additive-only backend deprecation. Diff is 199 lines across 4 source and 4 test files, following existing per-credential-type router-guard pattern (LiteLLM/Git/Webhook precedent) and existing model-field-addition pattern. Pre-commit hook (ruff + tests + sonar) green; 51 targeted tests green including new coverage. Three-lens review returned 7 nominally-major findings; all triaged as dismiss/defer after verification:

- 2 findings on `Optional[bool] = False` typing: matches the existing field-declaration convention throughout ToolMetadata/Tool (`Optional[str] = ''`, `Optional[bool] = False`); tightening it would deviate from local style with no runtime benefit given the default. Dismiss.
- 1 finding on serialization surface: the field is intentionally exposed in `GET /v1/tools` per AC1; not-excluding is the requirement, not a defect. Dismiss.
- 1 finding on message wording ("read-only"): the block on POST+PUT is exactly what makes existing rows read-only; message is accurate. Dismiss.
- 2 findings on guard ordering (before ownership/project-access checks): deprecation is universal and by design credential-type-driven; no data disclosure (tool catalog is public via `GET /v1/tools`). Dismiss.
- 1 finding on PUT bypass by omitting `credential_type`: false positive; `credential_type: CredentialTypes` is a required Pydantic field on `SettingRequest`, so a body without it is rejected with 422 before reaching the guard. Verified against src/codemie/rest_api/models/settings.py:225. Dismiss.
- 1 finding on test style (using `pytest.raises(ExtendedHTTPException)` rather than asserting on the ASGI response envelope): established project convention — every existing router-test in test_user_settings.py / test_project_settings.py uses this pattern. Defer as a broader project-wide test refactor.

0 blocking findings survive.
